title: Assessing Recovery Potential of a Reintroduced Lake Sturgeon Acipenser fulvescens Population in the Southeastern United States
content:
ABSTRACT

We assessed a reintroduced population of Lake Sturgeon, Acipenser fulvescens, in the Coosa River, Georgia, that was extirpated for approximately 30 years. We used mark-recapture data and field observations to quantify dynamic rate functions and characterize life history attributes. Results indicated that multiple year classes of stocked Lake Sturgeon successfully grew and established a population. Lake Sturgeon grew quickly and began to asymptote to an estimated mean maximum length (L∞) of 1218 mm (±56 mm; 95% CI) and age of 34 years (±6 years; 95% CI). Lake Sturgeon were in good body condition, with a modified form factor of 5.40. We documented sexual maturation as early as age 12 for males, although age at maturation could not be quantified for both sexes. Our results suggest a robust population exhibiting rapid growth, early maturation, and growth and longevity potential that may be lower than in northern populations. Collectively, these data inform management and fill knowledge gaps regarding Lake Sturgeon population dynamics at the southern extent of their range.
